examples.question_text:
Name the main bias in each method and explain.
(a) To find all students’ favourite sport, a school asks only its basketball team.
(b) A council puts a vote on its website and waits for residents to choose to reply.
examples.solution_text:
(a) **Selection bias**: basketball players are over-represented and may favour basketball more than students in general.
(b) **Volunteer bias**: residents choose whether to reply. Those with strong opinions may be more likely to take part.

examples.question_text:
Name the main problem with each sample.
(a) A factory studies how long its machines last by inspecting only machines still working after ten years. Machines that failed earlier were scrapped.
(b) To find the views of $420$ residents, a council asks only $2$ of them.
examples.solution_text:
(a) **Survivorship bias**: the machines that failed early are missing, so only the survivors are studied.
(b) **Small sample size**: two residents may not show the range of views in the town.

examples.question_text:
Identify the fault and rewrite each question fairly.
(a) "Do you agree that our brilliant new library should stay open?"
(b) "How often do you visit the library?"
examples.solution_text:
(a) **Leading question**: "brilliant" praises the library and pushes towards agreement. A fair version is "Should the new library stay open?"
(b) **Ambiguous question**: no time period is given. A clearer version is "How many times did you visit the library in the past week?"

examples.question_text:
Explain the problem in each survey and suggest an improvement.
(a) A service rating offers only Good, Very good and Excellent.
(b) Spending groups are $\$0$–$\$10$, $\$10$–$\$20$ and $\$20$–$\$30$, with both ends included.
(c) A club says $4000$ voluntary online replies cannot be biased.
examples.solution_text:
(a) **Not enough choices**: unhappy customers have no suitable answer. Include negative and neutral ratings as well as positive ones.
(b) **Overlapping choices**: $\$10$ and $\$20$ each fit two groups. State boundaries so each amount fits only one group, and allow amounts outside the listed range.
(c) A large number does not remove **volunteer bias**. Choose members at random from the full membership list and contact them directly instead of relying only on voluntary online replies.
